text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The South African government is genuinely committed to entering into a bilateral trade agreement with Zimbabwe, despite delays in implementing the pact, South African Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said on Monday at the opening of a two-day meeting of the Zimbabwe-South Africa Joint Commission.
- Zimbabwe's state National Security Authority (NSSA) will invest Z$600 million in housing in the next five years, National Construction and Housing Minister Enos Chikowore said.

- Four leading commercial banks -- Standard Chartered Bank Zimbabwe, Barclays Bank Zimbabwe, Zimbabwe Banking Corporation (Zimbank) and Commercial Bank of Zimbabwe -- are refusing deposits into accounts of savings accounts that have sprouted around the country in the past few months. Bank officials say there are no laws governing the operations of the savings clubs.
